title: High-flow Nasal Oxygenation in Obese Patients During Colonoscopy: a Randomized Controlled Trial (COCOON)
official: High-flow Nasal Oxygenation in Obese Patient During Colonoscopy: a Randomized Controlled Trial: the COCOON Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether high-flow oxygen therapy (HFOT) is more effective than conventional oxygen therapy (COT) in reducing episodes of intraoperative oxygen desaturation (oxygen saturation \[SpO2\] ≤ 90%) during colonoscopy under general anesthesia in adults with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² or higher.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Does high-flow oxygen therapy reduce the occurrence of intraoperative oxygen desaturation compared with conventional oxygen therapy during colonoscopy under general anesthesia? Researchers will compare high-flow oxygen therapy with conventional oxygen therapy to determine whether high-flow oxygen therapy reduces the occurrence of intraoperative oxygen desaturation.

Participants will:

Be screened during their anesthesia consultation between 60 days and 48 hours before the scheduled colonoscopy.

Be randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either conventional oxygen therapy or high-flow oxygen therapy. Receive standard monitoring and 3 minutes of pre-oxygenation according to their assigned treatment group.

Undergo colonoscopy under general anesthesia while breathing spontaneously. Be monitored for oxygen desaturation during the procedure. Have ventilatory and hemodynamic data recorded during the procedure and collected immediately after the colonoscopy.

The study will include adults scheduled for a colonoscopy at Bichat-Claude Bernard Hospital, Beaujon Hospital, or Louis Mourier Hospital.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older.
* Body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² or higher.
* Scheduled to undergo a colonoscopy under general anesthesia with spontaneous breathing at Bichat-Claude Bernard Hospital, Beaujon Hospital, or Louis Mourier Hospital.
* Affiliated with a social security scheme.
* Free, informed and written consent signed.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Colonoscopy in a participant at high risk of aspiration requiring orotracheal intubation, defined by at least one of the following:

  * Symptomatic or severe gastroesophageal reflux disease, notably with frequent regurgitation (≥ 2 episodes per week), mainly occurring in the supine position;
  * Hiatal hernia;
  * History of bariatric surgery (sleeve gastrectomy, gastric bypass);
  * Neurodegenerative disease requiring airway protection during colonoscopy.
* Emergency colonoscopy.
* Chronic respiratory failure.
* Severe heart failure.
* Allergy to propofol.
* Pregnant or breastfeeding woman.
* Adult under legal protection (guardianship or curatorship).
* Beneficiary of State Medical Aid (Aide Médicale de l'État, AME).
